A.explanation: Decreasing the time-base stretches the trace horizontally so even less of the cycle fits, and decreasing the y-gain in $\text{V cm}^{-1}$ would be correct vertically but not with the time-base change.

B.explanation: Decreasing the time-base increases the time stretch, so the already too-wide waveform would extend further beyond the screen width.

walkthrough: Look at the given trace: it enters at the left edge below the top, rises off the top of the screen, and only re-enters near the right edge. The peak is cut off and far less than one sinusoidal cycle is spread across the width.

Recall the CRO controls: time-base sets time per horizontal division in $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ and y-gain sets voltage per vertical division in $\text{V cm}^{-1}$. Increasing the number per division compresses that axis.

Horizontally, the waveform is too stretched because one period occupies more than the screen width. Increase the time-base $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ so more time fits across the screen and one full period $T$ can be displayed.

Vertically, the amplitude is too large because the top of the wave is off scale. Increase the y-gain $\text{V cm}^{-1}$ so each vertical centimetre represents more volts and the peak is brought back onto the screen.
Both changes together shrink the image to a continuous sine wave showing one complete cycle. This is option D.
